title: Seen a ghost? Start with curiosity, not fear
excerpt: A ghost guide shares how to explore unexplained encounters responsibly — and when to check for ordinary causes first.
content:
GHOST GUIDE

Have you seen a ghost? Rebekah Carmichael says curiosity, not fear, is the place to start

TikTok medium Rebekah Carmichael discusses her new book, 'The Not-So-Scary Guide to Ghosts' and offers advice on paranormal experiences, spirit communication and checking practical explanations first.

Have you ever been touched by a hand that wasn't there? Heard unexplained footsteps? Seen something out of the corner of your eye? 

Read It

"The Not-So-Scary Guide to Ghosts" by Rebekah Carmichael

Published by Adams Media, an imprint of Simon & Schuster

256 pages

$20

These experiences can be scary, but Rebekah Carmichael — known to her legions of fans on TikTok as Rebekah The Ghost Guide — believes they don't have to be. But first, she says, we have to start talking about paranormal encounters as normal experiences. 

"There's a lack of understanding and so much mystery around this," Carmichael, who is a medium, said in a recent phone interview from Wilmington, N.C., where she once lived in a haunted house. "The scary part comes from people not wanting to talk about it."

Not wanting to talk about a paranormal experience — the possibility of having connected with a spirit or ghost — often comes from not knowing how to conceptualize it and put it into words. So instead, she said, we tell ghost stories.

While storytelling is important to a shared communal experience, she thinks talking about the paranormal, as we do anything else, has more benefits. 

"It's in sharing experiences, in putting ourselves out there, that we share understanding and ultimately fight fear," Carmichael said. 

That's where her new book, "The Not-So-Scary Guide to Ghosts: How to Make the Paranormal Normal," comes in. 

It's the practical guide to spirit communication and mediumship she wishes she'd had when she was first starting on her own journey with the supernatural — a journey that she now knows began in her childhood, but she didn't embrace until she was an adult. 

"For me, I've had a lot of experiences. I sought out other people to meet. I was convinced I was not the only person to have spiritual experiences and be able to talk to them and that sort of thing. I needed to find my community. So, I put myself out there," she said. In doing this, she not only found a community, but also a group of people who were looking for guidance. 

"I found so many who said, 'I want to do what you do.' So, I looked back at my life. I asked myself: How many times did I need something? What did I need? What could I have provided myself in the past that will directly be able to be applied by people, starting from any direction, when they're looking at a paranormal? And that's how this book came about."

The guide intersperses Carmichael's personal experiences with sections on ghosts and psychic mediumship, how to understand your own energy and shield yourself, how to sense spirits and start a conversation with one and how to validate your experiences with tools and share your encounters.

Carmichael recently took the time to talk with The Eagle and answer a few of our questions about how people who are curious about ghosts can communicate with them without it being scary. Her answers have been lightly edited for length and clarity.

1 In your book, you distinguish between being curious about an experience and being afraid of it. How did you learn to make that shift yourself?

 Immersion. I willingly and unwillingly immersed myself in living in a very haunted place. I'm still living in Wilmington, N.C., for the most part; when I'm not on the road. There are spirits everywhere. There have been colonizers here since the 1600s, and of course, there are the Native people, who have been here long before that. There are just a lot of things that have happened here that are instrumental to our history as a country. All of that leaves a particular residue. It leaves a mystery. It leaves a curiosity.

At some point, I had to make the decision: I'm either going to live in my fear and not have answers or I'm going to pursue my fear and talk to people, learn the history and see what I can figure out when it comes to human behavior, whether it's incarnate or not. 

2 In your book, you describe intuition and psychic abilities as skills that can be used as tools for understanding paranormal experiences. How do you know when you're receiving information versus when your own expectations/imagination are filling in the blanks?

I wish there was a foolproof way. I wish I could be like, "That's absolutely psychic." It's practice. I tell people the difference between a psychic and everyone else is the psychic trains themselves to listen to the minute details that pop up in their brain. We're talking no train of thought, no physical thing around us as an indication of what we are seeing or experiencing.

3What does responsible spirit communication look like to you? And where do you think people can get themselves into trouble?

I believe that responsible communication with the spirit is truly no different from responsible communication with anyone else. Talk to them as you would any other person. 

Be aware of yourself and your feelings before going into a conversation. Projection, for example, is very common. When we're stuck in our own feelings, it's common to project them onto other people and entirely miss what they're saying. This happens in everyday physical conversations, and it's just as easy to do in spiritual conversations. 

When you understand your own thought process, your own feelings and how your day went can impact your conversations, that can be a fundamental difference in how you understand others around you, even in the most simple conversations.

I apply that to spirits. I need to know myself first before I go and try to make sense of something I can't see with my physical eyes. That is the fundamental part of my teaching: Know yourself first before you try to understand something beyond yourself.

4One of the things that drew me to your book is the idea of making the paranormal “normal.” What changes when you stop treating a ghost as a scary story and start thinking about it as an encounter with another person — or another kind of consciousness?

You get to challenge your beliefs. I love that because I always want to learn and grow. And yes, that comes with discomfort.

5A lot of people will have an experience they can't explain and immediately start looking for a paranormal explanation. How do you suggest readers distinguish between something generally unusual and something that has a more ordinary explanation? 

I believe it's very important to check all the physical things first. You want to check your electrical. You want to make sure that it's not a gust of wind that's shaking your windows. Check for a gas leak. Gas leaks can cause paranoia. Not everybody has them, but if you do have a gas leak, you definitely want to know as quickly as possible and get it fixed.

Apply science, and then, if you really can't find anything, that's when you get to say, "Let's pull out the spiritual tools. Let's get out the recorders. Let's see what we can get." But I always want people to ground themselves and not just assume that everything is paranormal. Because when everything but the paranormal has been ruled out, it's even more exciting.
